narrative.overview: Rasvia looks like the interface a serious restaurant operator would trust at 4pm before dinner service: dark, legible, amber where action lives, no decorative noise. Marketing pages lead with the same voice as the partner dashboard — one brand, not a glossy landing site bolted onto a utilitarian admin panel.
keyCharacteristics: Amber accent used sparingly for CTAs, badges, and operational emphasis — not as wallpaper
Zinc neutrals with hairline borders instead of heavy drop shadows
8px base radius; cards at 12px; marketing CTAs at 12–16px
shadcn/ui primitives extended with dashboard tokens in lib/dashboardUi.ts
Product mockups on marketing pages stay dark-themed inside their shells

rules.name: The Compatibility Rule
rules.body: Light-theme slate remaps live only in index.css. Marketing uses marketingUi.ts zinc tokens.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only brand chroma on marketing and dashboard chrome. Status colors appear only on operational badges.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Display and headline letter-spacing never tighter than -0.04em.

rules.name: The No Ghost-Card Rule
rules.body: Never combine border: 1px solid with a wide soft drop shadow (blur ≥16px) on the same element.

dos: Do use amber for primary actions and operational emphasis only.
Do keep body copy at WCAG AA contrast.
Do use Bricolage Grotesque at weight 900 for marketing headlines with tracking ≥ -0.04em.
Do reuse DASH_* tokens from lib/dashboardUi.ts for dashboard actions.
Do show real product UI in marketing mockups.
donts: Don't use generic SaaS landing patterns: cream/beige body backgrounds, small uppercase eyebrow kickers above every section, identical icon + heading + text card grids.
Don't add gradient text for headlines.
Don't use side-stripe borders on cards, alerts, or list items.
Don't exceed 16px border-radius on cards and sections.
Don't pair 1px borders with wide soft shadows on the same element.
Don't introduce numbered section markers unless the section is a genuine ordered sequence.
